nodes.label: DEFERRED.md — cross-chapter deferral ledger
nodes.rationale: Append-only member recording every cross-chapter item deferred during Phase R2, one section per originating chat (74 through 148). It replaces the deferred paragraph of the handoff (chat 74, ruling 3) so that a deferral survives the chat that raised it rather than being carried in prose.

nodes.label: Append-only closure rule
nodes.rationale: "Do not re-derive; settle each item in the chapter named. An item is closed by a later line that cites the READ file closing it — never by deletion." Deletion would erase the evidence that an item was ever open, so closure is recorded as an addition citing its own witness.

nodes.label: Phase R2 — the section read
nodes.rationale: The reading pass that walks the main volume in line-bounded units and defers anything that cannot be settled inside the unit. R2 measures and records; it never repairs.

nodes.label: Phase R3 — the repair pass
nodes.rationale: The pass that will act on what R2 recorded. Items are routed to R3 marked 'for R3, no withdrawal' — the finding stands as measured and the decision about the text is R3's, not the reading chat's.

nodes.label: READ-chNN.md closing file
nodes.rationale: Each chat's read is written up in a READ file; a deferred item is closed only by a line citing the READ file that closed it, which makes the closure auditable back to a specific measurement.

nodes.label: The docket system
nodes.rationale: From roughly chat 120 onward the ledger stops listing loose items and routes each finding to a numbered docket ('Docket 34 gains…', 'Docket 37 loses…'). A docket is a standing class of defect, so a new finding accretes to an existing decision rather than opening a new one.

nodes.label: Docket 9(a) — misdirected pointer
nodes.rationale: A citation whose named target does not carry the cited content: §33 L9451's 'the indexes of §36' where §36 is 'Three bodies'; A.6's row sending adjunction-never-repairs to §24.2 when the theorem is §17.2. Measured by counting hits of the cited phrase in the resolved body, so the finding is a zero rather than an opinion.

nodes.label: Docket 9(b) — mis-ordinalled or miscounted criterion
nodes.rationale: A claim that names its place in an enumeration wrongly — L9486 calling 'Never fit across a language boundary' the fourth question of the domain protocol when register 1336's four questions do not include it.

nodes.label: Docket 9(c) / 30 — cited but absent Register numbers
nodes.rationale: Register numbers cited in the volumes with no entry seated. Re-measured as warn-04: reading grouped '### N, N, …' headings as well as bare '### N' moves the absent-and-cited class, so part of the class was an artefact of the reconstruction convention rather than of the Register.

nodes.label: Docket 10 — unreproducible uncertainty bracket
nodes.rationale: Printed ± half-widths (± 1,398, ± 1,594, ± 2,169) that match none of eight candidate bases; the bracket's construction is not printed and cannot be recovered from the page.

nodes.label: Docket 12 — statement stronger than its proof
nodes.rationale: A.13 states an 'iff' bound whose own proof holds only 'to leading order'; the fix is wording, not a figure move, since the numerals reproduce.

nodes.label: Docket 14 — roster contradiction
nodes.rationale: Two printed six-language rosters share only two names (§33.1 vs §20.2). Settled by site count across the Index of Indices rather than by authority: order 31, statistics 11, analysis 7, information 7, algebra 5, geometry 5 against calculus 0 and logic 1, so §20.2 is the outlier to repair.

nodes.label: Docket 15 — superseded figure still asserted
nodes.rationale: A retired value carried unmarked at later sites — 'nine of eleven closed indexes' standing at three sites after register 1347 fixed the population at twelve.

nodes.label: Docket 17 — figure with no Register site
nodes.rationale: A printed number resting on a single passage with nothing seated in the Register behind it; the claim may be true and is still unsourced.

nodes.label: Docket 19 — claim with no population
nodes.rationale: A comparative or statistical claim ('anticorrelated in nature', 'the one that blocks the most') for which no population or denominator is stated, so it is unmeasurable rather than wrong.

nodes.label: Docket 23 — sentence attributed to the wrong chapter
nodes.rationale: Its sharpest member is §33.3 L9449, which sits inside Chapter 33 citing Chapter 27 for a sentence whose verbatim home is register 1327 and whose current printing is Chapter 33. The repair text already exists: §35.1 was repaired the same way and now reads 'Chapter 33 said'.

nodes.label: Docket 34 — unprinted convention
nodes.rationale: The largest docket. A figure reproduces only under a convention the book never states — a rounding chain, an ambient box, a coordinate the record fixes by reproduction. The figure is right; what is missing is the rule that makes it right, so the repair is an entry naming the convention rather than a change to the number.

nodes.label: Docket 35 — a WARNING the citer does not carry
nodes.rationale: A Register entry marked WARNING is cited by a volume that reproduces the figure and drops the qualification; the citation then reads as settled where the record says it is not. R3's rule: each citer either restates the qualification or drops the citation.

nodes.label: Docket 36 — References and Index
nodes.rationale: Back-matter items: works cited in the body but absent from a References subsection or the Register, and Index rows whose entry count differs from its distinct-term count.

nodes.label: Docket 37 — a printed figure that does not reproduce
nodes.rationale: The docket that can lose members as well as gain them: chats 146 and 147 removed 23a-03 (i) and narrowed 24a-05 once the re-derivation was rerun under the volume's own operator instead of the reconstruction's.

nodes.label: Docket 38 — the original instrument is not a member
nodes.rationale: Where the code that produced a printed figure was never seated, the figure can only be re-derived, never reproduced; a mismatch then cannot distinguish a book fault from a reconstruction fault.

nodes.label: r2lib — the shared instrument library
nodes.rationale: Functions proven in one chat's instrument are lifted into r2lib verbatim by AST, with provenance comments, and only when a later segment actually needs them. Lifting on need rather than on sight keeps the library from accumulating untested API, and lifting verbatim keeps a later run comparable with the run that first produced a figure.

nodes.label: Verbatim lift with provenance
nodes.rationale: A function moves into r2lib unchanged and carrying a comment naming the instrument it came from; the ledger keeps a standing 'owed to r2lib' list across chats so nothing is silently rewritten on the way in.

nodes.label: Banked golden output (NAME.out)
nodes.rationale: Each instrument's stdout is seated as a golden member so a rerun is a comparison rather than a re-reading. Runtimes are recorded beside them (r2-ch12m ≈ 150 s, r2-ch13t ≈ 81 s) so a gate run list can be assembled by cost; r2-ch12c is deliberately not banked because it prints wall-clock time and so cannot reproduce.

nodes.label: ℛ / r2lib.Rset — the volume's own closure operator
nodes.rationale: §6.1 L1540's φ̂ᵢⱼ(v) = max{xᵢ : xⱼ ≤ v}, a running maximum over the ambient ∏ Âᵢ(X) of occupied value sets. Chat 146 fixed it as the scoring rule: an E figure is measured under the book's own operator before any rival reading, because a re-derivation that codes its own φ is a reconstruction and its disagreement is evidence about itself.

nodes.label: The equality-bound φ fault
nodes.rationale: r2-ch23a.py §4 and r2-ch24a.py §4 both bound φ by equality (max{xᵢ : xⱼ = v}) rather than by ≤, and both produced 'unreproducible' verdicts that reversed once the operator was corrected — the same fault twice, found a chat apart.

nodes.label: G0c — book right, instrument wrong
nodes.rationale: A verdict class for a non-reproduction that turns out to be the reconstruction's fault. It is what lets docket 37 lose members: the finding is retained as a record about the instrument rather than deleted, and the docket entry is reversed by measurement.

nodes.label: C9 discipline — no impossibility claimed
nodes.rationale: Where an object is undefined, the reading records that it cannot be checked rather than that the figure is wrong — 'a poset need not have all joins, so 511 may be a sub-count of a larger pair set'.

nodes.label: Rounding chain U versus chain P
nodes.rationale: Every figure of §25.6.1–4, §32.5.1 and E.3 reproduces with δ carried unrounded (chain U, 25 of 25); quantizing δ to the printed 4 dp (chain P) moves twelve by 1–7 in the last place. The book names neither chain, so a re-derivation is scored under both and the chain the book used is identified from the match.

nodes.label: Digit-bounded figure probe
nodes.rationale: A figure is searched with `(?<![\d.,])F(?![\d])` on both sides; an unbounded '1,520' matches Register 1303's '11,520' and manufactures a site that is not there.

nodes.label: The Method 1.6 main volume
nodes.rationale: Read by R2 in line-bounded units from L2385 to L11855, chapter by chapter, closing with the References at chat 141.

nodes.label: Mathematical Compendium (MC)
nodes.rationale: A companion volume that restates main-volume results; the ledger routes items to 'the MC pass' where MC inherits a finding by pointer, and records where MC is correct against a main-volume slip (MC L1264 on 'the largest 2J_c').

nodes.label: Index of Indices (IoI)
nodes.rationale: Used both as a volume to check and as the population that settles docket 14's roster contradiction by site count.

nodes.label: The Register
nodes.rationale: Append-only, which is why order matters for R3: a section written to satisfy nine existing Register citations must be written to what those entries already say, not the other way round. Its WARNING marks and its silences are themselves findings (docket 35, docket 17).

nodes.label: Λ — the tower and its stages Λ₈–Λ₁₃
nodes.rationale: The staged index the Chapter 12 readings measure against: cell counts (Λ₁₂ 70,905, Λ₁₃ 199,130), closure sweeps (47,775,744 at Λ₁₃) and ⟨q⟩ per stage.

nodes.label: E — the excess measure
nodes.rationale: |ℛ(X)| against |X| over a declared ambient. Its value depends entirely on what the ambient is taken to be — occupied value sets versus interval hull — which is why so many E disputes resolve into docket 34 convention items rather than arithmetic.

nodes.label: The constraint tree
nodes.rationale: Figure 12.4's object, 13 nodes and 14 edges in Register 1790 against 13 edges and one triangle from the table's bounds — the discrepancy is the f–K edge L3066 excludes, i.e. whether K has one parent or two.

nodes.label: The §14.5 authoring gap
nodes.rationale: Six headings (§14.5.2–§14.5.7) with zero body lines, identical in BUILD90 and in the Prints & Proofs original — so the text never existed at the input and no earlier print carries it. Forty citations in four volumes resolve to empty headings. Closed as a question, open as a repair, and R3's largest single item.

nodes.label: HANDOFF-25 (chat 74)
nodes.rationale: The handoff whose deferred paragraph this member replaces; its list is carried into DEFERRED.md verbatim as the ledger's opening state.

nodes.label: Ruling 45 — build and session remarks
nodes.rationale: Lines like 'the build now fails on any missing glyph' or 'a gzipped file this session could not read' are remarks about the production run, not claims about the subject, and are excluded from the defect count.

nodes.label: Ruling 46 — internal file references
nodes.rationale: Tokens such as (fig-sections) or (fig-tree) are build-internal references rather than broken citations, so they are not counted as misdirected pointers.

nodes.label: RUL-128 — the post-read work programme
nodes.rationale: After the main volume was read in full at chat 141, item 3 (ii) directs the non-section work: the Register WARNING sweep (chat 142), then the re-take families (chats 143–144). Its item 1 requires a Register entry to seat a derivation before any prose is touched.

nodes.label: DEF-143 item 11 — the re-derivation order
nodes.rationale: A fixed queue worked one family per chat, one instrument each, each banked: 21a-02/03, 23a-03, 24a-05, 25b-03, 26b-04, 26b-02/-03, 27a-02's seven entries, 28a-06, 28b-06. Each chat restates the remaining order so the queue survives the session that is working it.

nodes.label: Cowork environment findings
nodes.rationale: Measured, not assumed: a bundle delivered by SendUserFile is not in Materials until M uploads it, so the gate's title search finds zero and stops; Graphify's workspace indexes only Python symbols and cannot substitute for Materials; an inline Drive result is decoded byte-exact from the session transcript rather than re-typed.

nodes.label: r2-ch12f
nodes.rationale: Source of build9, src, tgt, leq, tarjan and analyse, lifted into r2lib at chat 74; supplies the 182,719 : 9,331 split and the cycle cells.

nodes.label: r2-ch12r
nodes.rationale: Carries L8_at / phi_at (the tower at arbitrary caps) and Rbox (|ℛ(X)| by ambient-box sweep, sliced for a 13-coordinate box); reproduces the 47,775,744-cell closure at Λ₁₃ in ≈ 25 s.

nodes.label: r2-ch13a
nodes.rationale: Measures the tight-K cuts (Λ₁₂ 70,905 → 55,755, Λ₁₃ 199,130 → 153,680) and settles the tower-table grading column per chain.

nodes.label: r2-ch13t
nodes.rationale: Computable Chapter 18 instrument, ≈ 81 s; defines failcount, parts and viol.

nodes.label: viol — non-monotonicity under five readings at once
nodes.rationale: Reports comparable pairs, covering pairs, unit steps, join-homomorphism failures and the projection over realised value tuples in one run. Reporting all five is what let 13t-04 be stated as 'no reading reproduces it' rather than 'one reading does not' — a negative over a space instead of a single miss.

nodes.label: bibcat (r2-ch13v) — the bibliography catalogue
nodes.rationale: Parses the main volume's References (L11503–L11855) into 103 entries across seven subsections carrying line, subsection, year and read-in-full flag; 99 dated entries from 1744 to 2026, 39 pre-1970. Closes a three-chat catalogue debt.

nodes.label: r2-ch18a
nodes.rationale: Appendix A instrument; carries body_range, rbody and lettered (a lettered-heading resolver the numeric resolver returns None for) and measures the A-row pointer resolutions.

nodes.label: r2-ch23a
nodes.rationale: Appendix D.5 instrument whose §4 bound φ by equality; its non-reproduction verdicts were reversed at chat 146.

nodes.label: r2-ch24a
nodes.rationale: Appendix E instrument; repeated r2-ch23a's equality-bound φ, and its 'unreproducible under D.4.2's ℛ' was the reconstruction's fault in 12 of 13 figures.

nodes.label: r2-warn
nodes.rationale: The Register WARNING sweep instrument; its §3 PHRASE regex over six members is the witness for warn-04's absent-and-cited class.

nodes.label: 13t-01 — Theorems 11.1 and 11.2 have zero sites
nodes.rationale: §18.1.3 disclaims 'Theorems 11.1 and 11.2', which occur nowhere in the six volumes, against Theorem 18.1 at three sites and 18.2 at seven. R3 must decide between a renumbering and two lost theorems — the measurement cannot choose.

nodes.label: 13t-04 — the 86 violations reproduce under no reading
nodes.rationale: §18.2 L4971 and A.11 L10020's 86 fails under fifteen readings (three definitions × five monotonicity senses) at three cap settings; Λ₈ gives 9,894 comparable and 384 covering. The figure cannot be disposed of until the definition is fixed, so it moves with 13t-05 and neither is repairable alone.

nodes.label: 13t-05 — ν printed two ways
nodes.rationale: ν is e − δ at three sites and n − δ at a fourth, with δ given as f − ℓ in two places and as a value rather than a coordinate function in a third. The definition ambiguity is what blocks 13t-04's arithmetic.

nodes.label: 13t-06 — the conserving poset is defined nowhere
nodes.rationale: The object carrying the chapter's only non-componentwise witness (28 of 511 joins) occurs at exactly two sites, both inside the section its own pointer sends the reader to. Recorded not identified: R3 must supply the definition before either figure can be checked, and under C9 no impossibility is claimed.

nodes.label: 13a-01 — the withdrawn 2,475 still standing
nodes.rationale: L3477 prints 'the 2,475 previously printed here is withdrawn' while L914, L2533, L3067 and L3434 carry it; L3434 additionally cites §A.15 and register 230, neither of which prints the figure. The cleanest instance of a retraction that did not propagate.

nodes.label: 13b-01 — 'the tight two-parent K' names two rules
nodes.rationale: The one-sided 2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f cuts 15,150 / 45,450; MC L1696's exact Wigner–Racah rule |2J_c−2f| ≤ 2K ≤ 2J_c+2f step 2 cuts 48,630 / 134,840. Every printed figure is exact for the one-sided form — and the form is never named at L3475, so the text is right and unattributed.

nodes.label: 13c-01 — item K open and closed in different units
nodes.rationale: §12.11.7 reports the 2J_c ≤ k question as still open; §12.11.0.6's heading reads 'Q item K, closed' and its body answers it. Measured, the bound fails at exactly four terms and at three occupancies — so 'four cases' and 'at every occupancy' are both exact, in different units. Reconcile the status and name the unit.

nodes.label: 13c-03 — Figures 7.2–7.5 do not exist
nodes.rationale: L3503 names four figures by a 7-series number; the four described are Figures 12.2–12.5 and the only 7-series figure in the main volume is Figure 7.1.

nodes.label: 13d-01 — §12.11.4 credited for §12.11.8's proof
nodes.rationale: Chapter 13 attributes the four-scheme identity and the 2.17-fold spread to §12.11.4, which contains neither; both are §12.11.8's, which itself cites §12.11.4 correctly. Register 455 inherits the same attribution, and the repair must separate 'scheme' from 'route'.

nodes.label: 13d-02 — eight nouns for one population
nodes.rationale: The 1,635 is exact as the Register's entry-heading count, but L3514 calls the entries 'withdrawals' where kinds.py classifies 33 as withdrawals; fifteen sites use eight different nouns for the same set. A self-description class: the book miscounts what kind of thing it holds, not how many.

nodes.label: 12v-02 — a broken correction chain
nodes.rationale: Register 625 attributes the withdrawn 50.3 % to Register 623, whose printed body says 0 % — so the chain that is supposed to record the correction does not connect at either end.

nodes.label: 12w-01 — the unstated Λ₁₁ matching rule
nodes.rationale: The rule taking the newest momentum as the target's fifth coordinate is never printed; the plain reading gives 0.8171 and breaks the section's no-exception claim. A docket-34-shaped defect found before the docket existed.

nodes.label: 12x-01 — a population named but printed nowhere
nodes.rationale: The 4,325-cell (Z, …) population is named in no member; the eight base counts and E = 972,862 / 28,503 are record-carried and not re-measurable, while every derived ratio is internally exact. R3 either rules the data into the record or rules Register 529's sourcing sufficient.

nodes.label: 21a-03 — 735,091 against 735,092
nodes.rationale: C.3's 'independent reproduction' reproduced a retired δ̄ row at a coarser Rydberg constant, not the live 736,688: 735,091 is exact at δ̄ = 0.99345, and 735,092 reproduces under R = 109,737 alone with no site outside C.3.

nodes.label: 23a-03 — D.5's E = 4 / E = 2, reversed by measurement
nodes.rationale: Docket 37 lost (i) outright — D.5.5's fibres reproduce 8 of 8 under the volume's own running-maximum operator, and the earlier failure came from the equality-bound φ. Part (ii) moved from a non-reproduction to a docket-34 unprinted convention: the page states 'measured' and 'sampled' but not the precedent, so the coordinates are fixed by reproduction rather than by print.

nodes.label: 24a-05 — Appendix E's E(Q) chain narrowed to one sentence
nodes.rationale: E.1.4's box 18 → 24 reproduces; the accompanying E 4 → 10 moves under none of four readings. Enumerating the 108/864 assignments of the unprinted coordinates leaves exactly one that reproduces every other printed figure, so the chain is recovered and only the +6 sentence's convention remains unstated.

nodes.label: warn-04 — the absent-and-cited class re-measured
nodes.rationale: Under grouped '### N, N, …' headings as well as bare '### N', numbers previously counted absent (219/220/221, 305, 239/256) are in fact headed. Every prior recording used the bare convention alone, so the finding is about the reconstruction; R3 decides whether a grouped heading satisfies a range citation.

hyperedges.label: Routing a finding: measure, docket, defer to R3
The reconstruction-fault family — when the instrument, not the book, is wrong
The Chapter 18 cluster — figures blocked by an undefined object
